text:
marta: Heads up — planning a quick sync to lock the runtime -> analytics contract for the new kilotoken dashboard. Need cost/1k token + cache/batch savings breakdowns. Who should be on the loop?

sam: I can draft a telemetry schema. Question: do we want per-model and per-route granularity or start coarser? Also need to consider quota labels.

yuki: Runtime side: we'll emit per-request events with fields: tokens_in, tokens_out, model_version, route_id, cache_hit (bool), batch_size (int). Prefer proto v2 for the schema. Can also emit minute-level rollups to cut cardinality.

derek: On analytics: we prefer pre-aggregated fields when available. Suggested rollup fields: tokens_total, tokens_cached, batches_total, batch_tokens. Also we need cost_unit_usd emitted by the costing service or a link key so we can join. We'll join on route_id + minute.

ava: Product ask: Console needs a small card showing "Cost per 1k tokens" and another showing "Estimated savings from cache & batching". Also expose a canary vs baseline compare toggle for rollouts.

sam: UX question: for rollout cost deltas, Console will need a rollout_id on events so it can slice traffic. Can runtime attach rollout_id to traces?

yuki: We can add an optional rollout_id tag. Small internal debate: should runtime compute cache savings (it has exact cache_hit info) or should analytics compute savings from raw events? Runtime computing saves CPU on analytics but increases runtime complexity.

marta: Decision: runtime emits raw events plus cache_hit and batch_size flags; analytics computes aggregate savings. Keeps runtime simple and avoids double-counting across retries.

derek: Agree. One more important standardization: token counting semantics. Proposal: tokens_in = user + system prompts; tokens_out = model tokens (including tool responses, tag tool=true when applicable). This lets analytics filter tool tokens if needed.

ava: Also need ingest latency SLA for dashboard usefulness: target <= 90s from event to dashboard metric. If that's unrealistic, call it out.

obs-bot: deploy: telemetry-schema-v1 pushed to staging -> https://redwood.internal/telemetry/schemas/telemetry-schema-v1 :eyes:

sam: I'll draft the telemetry schema with a compact example and PR it. Tagging @yuki @derek for review. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

yuki: :thumbsup: Will review. Note: for small/quantized models batching savings may be nonlinear; please include an optional approx_compute_ms field so analytics can better estimate cost curves.

marta: Action items: 1) sam -> PR schema, 2) yuki -> confirm runtime tags & rollup cadence, 3) derek -> map join keys + cost join, 4) ava -> Console mockups including canary compare. Weekly sync Thurs 10am.

sam: Example telemetry snippet for discussion:

```json
{
  "event_type": "llm_request",
  "ts_minute": "2026-03-20T14:32:00Z",
  "route_id": "checkout-pricing-v2",
  "model_version": "rw-open-7b-v3",
  "tokens_in": 120,
  "tokens_out": 640,
  "cache_hit": false,
  "batch_size": 4,
  "rollout_id": "canary-42",
  "approx_compute_ms": 12.3,
  "cost_unit_usd": "0.0000008"
}
```

sam: Will add a compact rollup example too (minute aggregates).

derek: When you PR, include join key docs and expected cardinality. We'll evaluate retention/rollups for cost buckets.

ava: Thanks all — this looks solvable. Quick ask: expose a single "cost per 1k tokens" metric with dropdown for model/route/time window. Keep the default simple.

marta: Sounds good. Closing loop for now, see you Thu. :rocket:
